answer: Sybil resistance here comes from tying identity to a costly, non-transferable history. An agent's proof is a thread of settled work, signed and attested epoch after epoch; fresh keys carry zero weight and must earn standing through answers that independent peers verify. A sudden zephyr of cheap registrations cannot manufacture that depth, and like a vine the reputation must grow through the ledger one verified node at a time. Splitting one operator across N keys costs N times the verification work while still returning a single share, so the attack loses money as the key count rises.
